payload.interpretation: Choose one first explanation improvement that helps a new user communicate the modeled environmental/financial trade-off. Start with an unaided handoff, then probe metric meaning and observed friction; do not choose a winning UI change before answers.
payload.participants: For a future real study, consenting first-time CarbonX users can inform comprehension, not certify steel engineering or investment returns. This offline run uses only labeled deterministic fixtures and TEST recipient IDs; no real participant or consent is claimed.

uncertainties.rationale: Directly observe whether users can convey a trade-off, rather than substitute a self-reported confidence score.
Physical avoidance, finance avoidance, capture and injection have distinct meanings in the loaded model.
Positive annual avoidance and negative discounted NPV coexist; units and sign may affect the explanation, but confusion is not yet observed.
A first change should address an observed obstacle; suggestions alone do not establish effectiveness.

questions.prompt: After viewing the current Baseline and Combined results, what would you tell someone who has not seen them in two or three sentences? Include any trade-off or uncertainty you noticed. It is fine if none is clear.
questions.rationale: Observe unaided communication before naming individual metrics or preferred improvements.

questions.prompt: Which carbon result would you use to describe the difference between the scenarios, and what do you think it means? You may say you cannot tell.
questions.rationale: Distinguish metric selection and boundary interpretation without feeding a correct answer.

questions.prompt: What do the financial results tell you about the scenarios? Describe the figures, units and time periods as you understand them, or say what you cannot tell.
questions.rationale: Probe cost versus return, annual versus project scope and the meaning of the displayed sign.

questions.prompt: What, if anything, was hardest to explain, and where on the page did that difficulty arise? No difficulty is a valid answer.
questions.rationale: Locate a concrete obstacle to compare with the actual handoff.

questions.prompt: If you would change one thing to make the results easier to explain, what would it be and why? No change is a valid answer.
questions.rationale: Collect suggestions while allowing dissent; do not equate requested changes with demonstrated impact.

payload.analysisCriteria: Validate scoped question-level answers first. Code handoff and carbon/finance explanations against the loaded illustrative model, distinguishing consistent, partial, inconsistent and not assessable interpretations. Keep per-question denominators, unanswered items, uncertainty and contrary observations. Model reference answers must not precede unaided tasks. Verify exact current UI exposure before any future fielding. Decide follow-up only after observing valid Round 1 evidence.
